title: Activities, the process, and where Compose fits in

videos.script: Your app never starts itself. The system starts it, and then tells it what is happening, and this lesson is about being told. {{activity}} First the activity: a class you write and never create. The system makes it, and calls six methods on it as the screen comes and goes. {{lifecycle}} Then you watch those calls, and not on a phone. A test drives the activity through Home, back again, and Back, and the log shows each step. {{rotation}} Then you turn the phone. The activity is destroyed and a new one is made, and whatever lived in the old one is gone, unless it was saved. {{process}} Then the hardest part to see. The system kills your whole process when it needs the memory, with no callback and no warning. And the user still expects the screen they left. {{compose}} Last, where Compose sits in all this: one view, inside one activity, with every screen of the planner drawn inside it.
